input.strategy_title: Feature Store as a supported RHOAI component
input.strategy_markdown:
## Problem Statement

Customers building recommendation and fraud models ask for a supported feature
store; today they self-manage upstream Feast next to the platform with no
lifecycle integration, no supported images, and no UI presence. Feast has a
Jira component reserved (Feature Store) but is not yet part of the platform:
there is no productized repository, no build pipeline, and no operator
integration. This strategy brings Feast in as a supported, installable RHOAI
component.

## High-Level Requirements

| ID | Priority | Requirement |
|-------|----------|-------------|
| HLR-1 | P0 | Administrators can enable a supported Feature Store (Feast) through the Platform Operator like any other managed component, with productized images. |
| HLR-2 | P1 | Data scientists can reach the feature store from workbenches with the Feast SDK preinstalled in at least one supported workbench image. |
| HLR-3 | P1 | The Dashboard shows the Feature Store as an enabled component and links users to its endpoints per project. |
| HLR-4 | P2 | Product documentation covers enablement, a getting-started walkthrough, and supported limits. |

## Affected Components

- Feature Store
- Dashboard
- Platform Operator
- Documentation

## Out of Scope

- A feature-authoring UI in the Dashboard (link-out only this release)
- Managed offline-store infrastructure — customers bring their own storage

## Open Questions

1. Which Feast deployment topology do we productize first — the operator-based
   deployment or the standalone server per project? Upstream supports both;
   supportability differs.

# Productize operator-based Feast deployment

## Description

Conditional branch: applies if the topology investigation selects the
operator-based deployment. Productize Feast for an operator-based deployment in
the midstream Feature Store repository — the deployment artifacts, custom
resources, and productized images that the Platform Operator will install and
manage. This epic exists only in this branch; the standalone-server equivalent
replaces it if the other outcome is selected.

## Scope

- Bring up the operator-based Feast deployment in the midstream repository:
  operator deployment artifacts, required custom resource definitions, and
  configuration for the managed deployment.
- Productize the required container images from the midstream repository.
- Adapt the upstream operator-based deployment for supported, productized use
  (defaults, lifecycle, upgrade behavior) as informed by the topology decision.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The operator-based Feast deployment installs and runs from the productized
  artifacts on the target OpenShift environment.
- Feast container images build green through the Konflux pipeline for this
  repository, with pinned image digests available for consumption by the
  Platform Operator enablement work.
- The deployment exposes the endpoint model recorded in the topology decision,
  confirmed against a deployed instance.
- Any upstream changes required for productization are identified and, where
  needed, submitted upstream or carried downstream with a documented disposition.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): delivers the productized deployment artifacts and images for
  operator-based enablement.

# Enable Feature Store via Platform Operator (operator topology)

## Description

Conditional branch: applies if the topology investigation selects the
operator-based deployment. Add the Feature Store to the Platform Operator as a
managed component so administrators can enable it like any other managed
component. This epic builds against the operator-based deployment artifacts
productized in this branch.

## Scope

- Add Feature Store enablement to the Platform Operator's managed-component
  framework for the operator-based topology: install/enable flow, default
  configuration, and lifecycle management of the Feast operator and its
  instances.
- Reference the productized Feast images by pinned digest (a configuration
  reference, not a build dependency).
- Provide enable/disable behavior consistent with other managed components,
  including a rollback path when the component is disabled.

## Acceptance Criteria

- An administrator can enable and disable the Feature Store through the Platform
  Operator like any other managed component.
- Enabling installs the operator-based Feast deployment from productized images
  with pinned digests, and the deployment becomes reachable per the topology
  decision's endpoint model.
- Disabling removes the Feature Store deployment cleanly (rollback path).
- The Platform Operator build pipeline is green with this change.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): full coverage of operator enablement with productized images for
  the operator-based topology.

# Select Feast deployment topology for productization

## Description

Resolve the strategy's open question: which Feast deployment topology Red Hat
productizes first — the operator-based deployment or the standalone server per
project. Upstream Feast supports both; supportability, deployment artifact shape,
endpoint granularity, and the Platform Operator integration all differ. This
investigation produces the decision that determines the structure of the Feature
Store deployment and enablement work.

## Scope

- Analyze both supported upstream topologies (operator-based deployment; standalone
  server per project) for supportability, lifecycle management, upgrade path, and
  fit with platform managed-component enablement.
- Determine the endpoint model each topology produces (per-project endpoints vs.
  shared/central endpoints) and its implications for Dashboard link-out.
- Assess upstream maturity and maintenance burden of each option (operator
  maturity, release cadence, OpenShift compatibility).
- Recommend one topology to productize first, with the decision recorded and
  accepted by stakeholders, and identify which conditional branch of downstream
  work it activates.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A decision document compares both topologies against explicit supportability
  criteria and records a single recommended topology.
- The recommendation states the endpoint granularity the chosen topology exposes
  per project, so Dashboard integration scope can be finalized.
- The decision is reviewed and accepted by the Feature Store stakeholders and the
  teams owning Platform Operator and Dashboard integration.
- Downstream deployment, enablement, and Dashboard integration scope is confirmed
  against the selected topology.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): gates the deployment productization and Platform Operator enablement
  work that delivers operator-based enablement with productized images.
- HLR-3 (P1): the chosen topology determines the endpoint model the Dashboard
  links to.

# Create midstream Feast repository under opendatahub-io

## Description

Provision the productized Feature Store code base: a midstream repository for
Feast under the opendatahub-io organization, following the same pattern as other
supported RHOAI components. This is the foundation for all downstream Feature
Store productization work — there is currently no productized repository.

## Scope

- Create the midstream Feast repository under opendatahub-io from the upstream
  source, following the midstream fork process used by other components.
- Establish branch structure, CI configuration placeholders, README, and ownership
  metadata consistent with other opendatahub-io midstream repositories.
- Set up the initial import of the upstream Feast source at the chosen baseline.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The midstream repository exists under opendatahub-io with the upstream Feast
  source imported at a recorded baseline.
- Repository metadata (owners, description, branch protection baseline) matches
  the conventions of other opendatahub-io component repositories.
- The repository is accessible to the Feature Store team for follow-on
  productization work.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): prerequisite for productizing Feast images and deployment artifacts.

# License validation for Feast and transitive dependencies

## Description

Run license validation over Feast and its transitive dependencies (server,
operator where applicable, and SDK packages) so that productization and the
workbench-image integration can proceed on a clean legal footing. Feature Store
is a new component, so no prior license scan covers it.

## Scope

- Scan the Feast upstream source and its transitive dependency tree for license
  compatibility with Red Hat product distribution.
- Cover the artifacts that will ship: the deployment/server components and the
  Feast SDK that will be preinstalled in a workbench image.
- Record findings and escalate any flagged dependencies for review; propose
  remediation (version change, exclusion, or documented exception) where needed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A license scan report covers Feast and its transitive dependencies for both the
  deployment components and the SDK.
- All flagged dependencies are resolved or have an approved documented disposition.
- The outcome is recorded so downstream implementation can proceed without
  license-driven rework.

## HLR Traceability

- HLR-1 (P0): productized images require a clean license position.
- HLR-2 (P1): the SDK preinstalled in workbench images must be license-cleared.

- A pipeline run completes and produces buildable Feast container images.
- Build status is visible to the team for follow-on releases.

## HLR Traceability

  (verification runs against an available deployment at execution time).
- The image addition follows the supported workbench image release process.
